name: Pennsylvania
metaDescription: Find Pennsylvania hunting dates for 2026–27, from deer and elk to turkey and migratory birds, plus license fees, education and draw deadlines.
homepageSummary: PGC season dates, WMU exceptions, fees and HuntFishPA deadlines.
intro: Pennsylvania’s dates are species-specific, and several seasons vary by Wildlife Management Unit (WMU). Deer and bear have statewide frameworks with exceptions, while fall turkey and migratory birds have distinct WMU or flyway-zone dates. Check the current digest before choosing a hunt.
zoneNote: Deer, bear and fall turkey rules can vary by WMU; waterfowl dates vary among North, South, Northwest and Lake Erie zones. Sunday hunting is generally included in 2026–27 seasons except migratory game birds, which remain closed Sundays.

licenseAndEducation.fact: The 2026–27 license year runs July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027; general hunting and trapping licenses went on sale June 22, 2026.

Buy online through HuntFishPA or in person from a PGC license issuing agent. Online delivery may take up to 10 business days, or 20 business days during high-sales periods; digital licenses do not include harvest tags.

Official prices: resident adult $20.97; resident junior $6.97 and junior combination $9.97; resident senior $13.97; nonresident adult $101.97; nonresident junior $41.97 and junior combination $51.97; nonresident 7-day small-game $31.97.

Resident archery $16.97, muzzleloader $11.97, migratory-game-bird $3.97, bear $16.97; nonresident archery $26.97, muzzleloader $21.97, migratory $6.97, bear $36.97; federal eDuck stamp $30.97; adult pheasant permit $26.97; snow-goose permit $1.97; bobcat/fisher/river-otter permits $6.97.
Antlerless license costs $6.97 resident and $26.97 nonresident. Scheduled 2026 rounds opened June 15, 22, July 13, 27, Aug. 10 and Aug. 24; remaining availability depends on WMU quotas in HuntFishPA.

The 2026 application ran May 1–July 12 through HuntFishPA. One $11.97 application allowed up to five season/zone/sex choices; drawing concluded July 25. A valid Pennsylvania general hunting license was required, including for nonresidents.

First-time hunters must complete Pennsylvania Basic Hunter-Trapper Education before obtaining a hunting license. In-person course is free; online options have stated fees. A score of at least 80% is required. Mentored hunters do not need the class before obtaining a mentored permit.
